chapter: The China offer, wedding and Shanghai
title: Japanese soldiers in Shanghai and getting out before the war
summary: He saw Japanese troops drilling in the streets, advised the band to leave, and the war broke out two weeks later, leaving Reginald Jones in a camp.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yes, there were American bands in the hotels. So, one morning after I came out, it must have been about 8 o'clock and we would ride the rik.shas, you know these .................... That's the first thing we did when we got to China was to get in a rik.sha and ride. These little guys pull them like horses. Snow, hot, it don't matter.

I was in a rik.sha coming home and I saw a Chinese fellow parked in his car waiting, he must have been waiting for somebody. After I'm around a building about ten Japanese ran up behind his car. They were doing maneuvers, right in the city, right in Shanghai these Japs, Japanese. They ran behind the car and pushed it like they were sneaking up on an enemy. And the poor little guy, he's sitting in there shaking to death, the little Chinese fellow.
And they pushed this car for about two blocks. Then they were through with it and
then they ran somewhere else. And they used to do that every morning right in, right in the middle of Shanghai in Shanghai you could see the Japanese soldiers.
Well, what were the Japanese soldiers doing there anyway?
They were there with the intentions of, eventually they were going to take over, China.
But was there a Japanese section of Shanghai?
There was, they had barracks there.
Oh, they did?

Yes. And I, after I told these fellows all of this, I said it's time, I think we should get out. They all had their money then. So everybody left home, I mean left bass man. He stayed there. And as no sooner I left, when I left about less than two weeks, the war exploded. They sent these gun boats right down in the middle of Shanghai and started shooting right into the city.
And everybody got out except Jonesy and he was put in a concentration camp. And he
still, he's out in Los Angeles today, he still has trouble with his legs where they, what they did to him, you know. But, he was in this Japanese camp.
Really?
Yes. Reginald, you know Reginald Jones? Renauld Jones, I mean.
Yes.
Trumpet player?
Yes.
That's his brother.
Oh really? Oh, I didn't know that.
That's his brother. So we got out.
How long would he have been in the concentration camp then?
I don't know.
I was just wondering how long that war went on.
I don't know. Well, it went on for some time.
Yes, but that was against China wasn't it? Not against, it wasn't against America?

Yes, it was against China. No, not that, not at that point. That came way late. But it eventually worked around to it, but it was just a beginning. But I was so glad that I left and everybody got out alright.
Sure.
But I don't know, I don't think I'd like to go back there now because it's not the same as it used to be.
